title.en: Modals — Can, Could, May, Might, Must, Should

headline.hi: Modals — Ability, Permission aur Necessity Dikhana

subtext.en: Can, Could, May, Might, Must, Should, Will, Would — all explained

text.en: Stop memorising modals one by one — see them as volume knobs and never mix up must/should/have to again.
text.hi: Modals ko ek-ek karke yaad karna band karo — inhe volume knobs ki tarah dekho aur must/should/have to mein confusion khatam.

content.en:
What are Modals?

Modals are 'helping verbs' that express ability, permission, possibility, necessity, advice, or request.

Golden Rule: After EVERY modal → always use V1 (base form)
• She can sing. (NOT 'can sings')
• He must go. (NOT 'must goes')
content.hi:
Modals kya hain?

Modals 'helping verbs' hain jo ability, permission, possibility, necessity, advice, ya request express karte hain.

Golden Rule: Har modal ke baad → hamesha V1 (base form)
• She can sing. ('can sings' NAHI)
• He must go. ('must goes' NAHI)

content.en:
🎚️ Modals Are Volume Knobs, Not Switches

Don't think of modals as separate words to memorise. Think of each GROUP as a volume knob you turn up or down:

Permission knob: Can (casual, low) → Could (polite, medium) → May (formal, high)
Possibility knob: Might (30% sure) → May (50% sure) → Must (95% sure, near-certain)
Obligation knob: Should (soft advice) → Have to (external pressure) → Must (strongest, no-choice)

Once you see modals as a DIAL rather than separate boxes, choosing the right one in an exam becomes: "how strong does this sentence feel?" — then pick the modal at that strength.
content.hi:
🎚️ Modals Volume Knobs Hain, Switches Nahi

Modals ko alag-alag yaad karne wale words mat samjho. Har GROUP ko ek volume knob ki tarah socho jise tum kam ya zyada karte ho:

Permission knob: Can (casual, low) → Could (polite, medium) → May (formal, high)
Possibility knob: Might (30% sure) → May (50% sure) → Must (95% sure, almost certain)
Obligation knob: Should (soft advice) → Have to (bahar se pressure) → Must (sabse strong, no-choice)

Ek baar modals ko alag boxes ki jagah ek DIAL ki tarah dekhna shuru karo, exam mein sahi modal choose karna ho jayega: "ye sentence kitna strong feel hota hai?" — phir uss strength ka modal pick karo.

content.en:
CAN vs COULD

CAN = Present Ability / Informal Permission
• I can swim. (present ability)
• Can I use your pen? (informal permission)

COULD = Past Ability / Polite Permission / Possibility
• I could swim when I was five. (past ability)
• Could I use your pen? (more polite)
• It could rain tomorrow. (possibility)

Memory Trick: CAN = abhi ki baat | COULD = pehle ki baat ya zyada polite
content.hi:
CAN vs COULD

CAN = Present Ability / Informal Permission
• I can swim. (present ability)
• Can I use your pen? (informal permission)

COULD = Past Ability / Polite Permission / Possibility
• I could swim when I was five. (past ability)
• Could I use your pen? (zyada polite)

Memory Trick: CAN = abhi ki baat | COULD = pehle ki baat ya zyada polite

content.en:
MAY vs MIGHT

MAY = Formal Permission / Strong Possibility (50% chance)
• You may leave now. (formal permission)
• It may rain today. (strong possibility)

MIGHT = Weak Possibility (30% chance) / Polite Suggestion
• It might rain today. (weak possibility)
• You might want to check your answers. (polite suggestion)

Key Difference: MAY = zyada chance | MIGHT = kam chance
content.hi:
MAY vs MIGHT

MAY = Formal Permission / Strong Possibility (50% chance)
• You may leave now. (formal permission)
• It may rain today. (strong possibility)

MIGHT = Weak Possibility (30% chance) / Polite Suggestion
• It might rain today. (weak possibility)
• You might want to check your answers. (polite suggestion)

Key Difference: MAY = zyada chance | MIGHT = kam chance

content.en:
MUST vs SHOULD vs HAVE TO

MUST = Strong Necessity / Obligation / Certainty
• You must wear a helmet. (rule/law)
• He must be tired. (certainty)

SHOULD = Advice / Recommendation
• You should study daily. (advice)
• You should see a doctor. (recommendation)

HAVE TO = External Obligation
• I have to wear a uniform. (school rule — external)
• I must obey my parents. (internal duty)

Memory Trick: MUST = karna HI padega | SHOULD = karna CHAHIYE | HAVE TO = kisi ne kaha, karna PADEGA

• He must be tired. (certainty)

SHOULD = Advice / Recommendation

HAVE TO = External Obligation

Memory Trick: MUST = karna HI padega | SHOULD = karna CHAHIYE | HAVE TO = kisi ne kaha, karna PADEGA

content.en:
WILL vs WOULD

WILL = Future / Promise / Instant Decision
• I will help you. (promise)
• I will take tea. (instant decision)

WOULD = Past Habit / Polite Request / Imaginary
• I would play cricket every evening. (past habit)
• Would you help me? (polite request)
• I would buy a car if I had money. (imaginary)

Memory Trick: WILL = abhi/aage | WOULD = pehle ki habit ya polite request

content.en:
🥊 Confusion Buster — MUST vs SHOULD vs HAVE TO

This trio confuses everyone because all three feel like 'you need to do this' — but the SOURCE of the pressure is different.

Ask: "Where is this rule coming from?"
• From ME, internally (my own decision/opinion) → MUST: "I must call my grandmother today." (I decided this matters)
• From SOMEONE ELSE, externally (school rule, law, boss) → HAVE TO: "I have to wear a uniform." (the school decided, not me)
• It's just good ADVICE, not a rule → SHOULD: "You should drink more water." (recommendation, no real consequence if ignored)

Exam shortcut: If the sentence mentions a LAW, RULE, or ORDER from an authority → have to. If it's the speaker's own strong feeling → must. If it's a suggestion → should.
content.hi:
🥊 Confusion Buster — MUST vs SHOULD vs HAVE TO

Ye teeno sabko confuse karte hain kyunki teeno 'tumhe ye karna hai' jaisa feel dete hain — but pressure kahan se aa raha hai wo alag hai.

Poocho: "Ye rule kahan se aa raha hai?"
• MERE andar se, internally (mera apna decision/opinion) → MUST: "I must call my grandmother today." (maine decide kiya ki ye important hai)
• KISI AUR se, externally (school rule, law, boss) → HAVE TO: "I have to wear a uniform." (school ne decide kiya, maine nahi)
• Ye bas achhi ADVICE hai, rule nahi → SHOULD: "You should drink more water." (recommendation, ignore kiya toh koi real consequence nahi)

Exam shortcut: Agar sentence mein LAW, RULE, ya ORDER kisi authority se mention hai → have to. Agar speaker ki apni strong feeling hai → must. Agar suggestion hai → should.

notes.en: ❌ She can sings well. → ✅ She can sing well. — Modal ke baad hamesha V1 (base form) aata hai.
